close_reason:
Refactored PushSubscriptionPatch to use Patch<T>:
- types: Patch<&[&str]> (was Option<&[&str]> + clear_types: bool)
- chat_push: Patch<&[(&Id, ChatPushConfig)]> (was Option<...> + clear_chat_push: bool)

Dropped the clear_* bool fields and the corresponding mutual-exclusion runtime checks — the invalid state is now unrepresentable at the type level. Handler emission switched to match Patch::{Keep, Clear, Set}; using-capability gate now checks !patch.chat_push.is_keep(). Debug impl trimmed of the removed fields.

API break is acceptable per pre-1.0 status and explicit bead authorization. Workspace grep clean (no other usages of clear_types/clear_chat_push). Tests, rustdoc, and clippy all green.

Committed as 0de0a70.
description: src/methods/mod.rs:1244-1266. PushSubscriptionPatch carries `clear_types: bool` and `clear_chat_push: bool` as separate fields, with mutual-exclusion validation at runtime in misc.rs:293-303. The crate's own Patch<T> machinery (mod.rs:124-187) exists specifically to eliminate this hazard — Patch<&'a [&'a str]> for `types` would make the (clear=true + Some(slice)) case unrepresentable at the type level. Today a caller can construct an invalid patch and only learn at request time. Fix: refactor to Patch<&[&str]> for types and Patch<&[(&Id, ChatPushConfig)]> for chat_push. Trade-off: requires Patch to handle slice types — but the same idiom is already used for Patch<&Id> elsewhere in mod.rs. Worth a public-API break before publishing.
title: PushSubscriptionPatch uses bool clear flags instead of Patch<T>
